Can you please just try to remember paragraph 6 of this report and the assessment mentioned therein? It should be the last page of the document. The assessment concerning the situation in Bugojno reads: "It appears that the BH army will win this battle over the near term. The estimate is over the next 48 hours, and will continue to press on towards Gornji Vakuf and perhaps even as far as Prozor." Do you remember this comment, and do you remember this particular assessment, sir?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically, I cannot remember that assessment because I didn't have any personal impressions of Bugojno. When we went through Bugojno, then there was no fighting going on any more. Otherwise, we wouldn't have been able to go through. Possibly, but I can't sure -- say for sure whether this -- this had already finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Speaking of this other area which you discussed at your meeting with Mr. Stojic, which is the southern part, rather, the possibility of a BH army attack coming from the south, could we please now go to a different document, which is another OTP document, 03563. The report is dated the 19th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please go to paragraph 5. It says: "Southern Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me just ask you whether you're familiar with these events. Number one reads: "On the 13th of July the BH started its own offensive from the south of down the direction of Blagaj and towards Buna and Gubavica. At the same time as this offensive, fighting broke out in many of the villages to the south of Mostar in the Capljina-Stolac area. The BH made initial gains, but the HV and HVO launched a counter-offensive." Sir, do you remember these events and do you remember these reports? Can you confirm that you received this report at the time and that they were indeed aware of all these activities?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only knew about these activities because of the reports, because we didn't have our personal impressions, although at that moment in time the team M3 that used to work there, although they -- they had a report on this, they heard about further fighting going on, but they were not close to it either. They were relatively far away. But they heard about fighting activities. That's all I can say about this. Everything else has been based on reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. This is the analysis of these events, and everything I've been asking you about was in one way or the other mentioned at your meeting with Mr. Bruno Stojic. At the very end of this analysis let me ask you this: The purpose of your meeting with Mr. Stojic on the 5th of July, 1993, was to obtain permission for your team to drive into Mostar. Therefore, could you please go to my binder and look for P 3362. This is the pink binder which the usher has probably provided for your benefit. Please go to document 3362.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you found it? Fine. The date is the 3rd -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] The first document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The number -- yes, yes. You're quite right. That's the first one in your binder, because your binder contains only those documents that I'm going to use. In the Judges' binder it's a different document. This report is dated the 10th of July, 1993. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's a report of the PMEZ, I see that you have it. It says coordination centre, Mostar coordination centre. That is under 2; right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we please have a look at this area of responsibility of the Mostar coordination centre. That's page 1 of the report. Number 2, it reads: "According to SpaBat, Mr. Boban said that UNPROFOR, UNMO, and ECMM would not be able to enter Mostar for at least another month. Team M2 tried to enter the city today but was denied access." The latter part is not entirely unsubstantial, but it is for the present question. Can you remember being told about this on or about the 10th of July, 1993, sir?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do think that the M2 team had tried again to get into Mostar at this time. Normally the check-point 20 kilometres east of Siroki Brijeg, because this was the daily practice, to try again and again. They might succeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My question was this, sir: Did you know or do you remember being told by SpaBat about what Mr. Boban had stated, namely that UNPROFOR, the UN military observers and the ECMM would not be allowed access to Mostar before a month's time. You tried to gain access yourself, and that's why I would like to know whether at any point you found out about this conversation with Mr. Boban, and did he indeed impose this veto or specify how long the veto would apply for?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't have remembered something like that, such a detail. I didn't hear this directly. If I heard, it was through a SpaBat report, but about this I really don't know any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that Mr. Boban was at the time the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know that, but I didn't meet him personally, although I was in Grude with Mr. Pogarcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now that you brought it up, can you tell me what Mr. Pogarcic's position was at the time? I mean at the time you met him.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he -- at the first meeting he said of himself that he was -- consulted Mr. Mate Boban in foreign policy matters, and he said why, because he spoke excellent English, because he obviously had spent many years in the North American area, could be Canada or the United States.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that at this critical time that we are talking about was also the chief commander of the HVO, the military component, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you mean that he had taken over the functions of Mr. Prlic or Mr. Soljic, then I don't know. That's something new to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you a very explicit question, but if you're not familiar with the set-up, then we'd best just leave that aside. I asked you very explicitly did you know that Mr. Boban was the chief commander of the HVO. If you didn't know anything about the set-up, I'd guess we'd best just leave that aside is then.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know that Mr. Mate Boban was the person who created Herceg-Bosna and automatically he was the supreme authority of the HVO. So what I -- whether he had taken over command or not, that would be something new to me. But I would say in rough terms that he had the say. I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Fine. That's precisely the answer I wanted to receive. Were you back in the area in 1994, sir? You also said that until the very end of your term there your own monitors, the monitors that were part of your mission, never gained access to East Mostar. Later on when you came back, did you ask any questions about when they eventually gained access, how, and who took the final decision? Did you want to know about that, and did you eventually learn anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean looking back to -- starting in 1994 and looking backwards, if I've understood you correctly, whether I was again in this area. The question, I must say, is something which I can't answer in such detail. I talked with the German monitor in great detail who was in Mostar in the winter as a monitor from Siroki Brijeg. But the question whether they could -- when they could go back in again, I can't remember. I don't remember whether we spoke about that. We talked about other things. For example, that they had been sending supplies in by aircraft and dropping them, because he had been a parachutist. So -- but this resumption of the access, this is something that I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I will do my best to refresh your memory, sir. If you can remember, fine. If not, let's just move on. Please have a look at Document P 05091, which is also the last document in my binder, the third document. 05091. Please tell me as soon as you've found it, sir.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Indeed. My German is that good, I must say. Can you please go to page 2 of that document, which reads "Annex." In the Croat version this is page 3. This appears to be a letter by Mr. Tadeusz Mazowiecki to the Secretary-General dated the 6th of September, 1993. Would you please just go briefly through page 3, which is the very next page in both Croatian and English. If you could look at number 2, please, item 2. I'll just read it briefly. "On the 18th of August, 1993, the Special Rapporteur expressed his concern on account of the situation, the situation described in Mostar and East Mostar. In his letter to Mr. Mate Boban, president of Bosnia's Croats, at the International Conference on the Former Yugoslavia, he exerted pressure on him to allow direct and unhindered access." I think you have it on your screen now. "... For humanitarian agencies and also his own human rights field officers. He later received a reply from Mr. Boban and access for the field staff was granted." Since this is a Security Council document, for that reason, among others, I wanted to ask you whether you've seen this document, or perhaps you were told by someone at some point that eventually the monitors and humanitarian agencies were allowed access, specifically allowed access by Mr. Boban. Do you remember that? If not, please let's not dwell on this any longer.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of this report really nothing. I don't know about this special matter as far as Mostar is concerned, but I do know that from the preparatory time of the visit of Mr. Mazowiecki, and from my visits in the Jablanica area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please go back to 3410. It's an OTP document and it's in the OTP binder. P 03410.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just two matters, sir, quite substantial ones. As you were being

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Stojic attended as well. If you could please go back to this document, in particular the section under the word "Subject." Could you go through the whole document perhaps, please, swiftly, in order to remember whether Mr. Bozic was the only one who attended that meeting and not Mr. Stojic, in fact. There is not a single reference in this document to Mr. Stojic as attending the meeting.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now that you've pointed that out to me again, I believe that it was as follows: On the 5th of July, there was my meeting with Mr. Stojic, and we agreed on the 10th of the 11th to have other meetings. And then I think on the 10th no meeting took place. On the 11th then with those people from Zagreb. Discussion with Mr. Bozic in Siroki Brijeg. Mr. Stojic was not there now that you point that out to me. But I'm a little unsure. But the report was written at the time. I must say that. If the report was written at the time, then of course the report is more telling than my memory, because I could have forgotten something in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: THE OTP
utterances.text: Could we perhaps simplify this. You're uncertain today whether Mr. Stojic attended the meeting or not. Can we decide that the report must be accurate in that case and that Mr. Bozic was the only person that attended?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I think that must have been the case. It couldn't have been otherwise. I wrote this in the evening. If the report is written by Mr. Martin Garrod, we wouldn't have written down anything wrong. If Mr. Stojic had been there, we would have seen that. But from my memory, it was no longer possible to say accurately.

utterances.speaker: THE OTP
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember at all while you were in Mostar, and you were in touch a lot with Mr. Bozic, that in addition to being the deputy chief of the defence department he also played a role in communication with international agencies, including yourself? Do you remember anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this second function, according to my memory, no expression was made of this expressis verbis but this only came to my attention from papers I read. I experienced this later. I don't recall that this was an actual subject.

utterances.speaker: THE OTP
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like now finally to go back to a question about the participation of the Croatian army and documents about the existence or non-existence of the Croatian army on the territory in which you had occasion to meet them or not meet them. So in order to do that, let's look at P 03710. It's a Prosecution document, and it's at the end of the Prosecution binder. The Prosecutor showed it to you today. We've already looked at that document.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the document of the 30th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE OTP
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. Now, the Prosecutor showed you some passages, but let's just confirm what your position is, because I assume that this is your definitive opinion about what you had an opportunity of seeing. So you compiled this report at the end of your mission there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OTP
utterances.text: I'm going to read out some portions. Under number 1 you say: "During my time as CC Mostar from the 1st of April to now, our teams had a permanent task to observe/monitor the HV involvement in BiH. It was obvious and confirmed that in past months the HVO used individual HVO soldiers, cars, and some weapons. It was not observed that any organised HVO troops, units from the platoon level upwards, and men, weapons, cars, symbols, leaders, had been moving around fighting, resting, or whatever else, engaged in any other activity." Now, you go on to say that you weren't allowed to work at night, but you go on to say that you did not notice any traces on the ground which we as soldiers would have been able to interpret. And I can't say how many HV soldiers there were in my area, but they were scattered around, and the team was not able to move around freely at times. And that would be my final question to you, sir. If I understand this correctly, what you're saying is this: You said that you saw individual soldiers here and there, but nowhere did you see nor could you notice that there were any units from platoon level upwards. You didn't notice any of that. You didn't notice any weapons, any cars or symbols or leaders. Am I right in making that conclusion from what I read in this report of yours?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. My monitors and myself saw it as it was.

utterances.speaker: THE OTP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That concludes my cross-examination. I'll now cede the floor to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Nozica. Next Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'll be the next one to cross-examine the gentleman. If we could have our break. I need about five minutes to set up, and I think it would be appropriate, and then we could just finish off for the rest of the session, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have a 20-minute break. We'll resume at half past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Michael Karnavas, and with me is Suzana Tomanovic, and we represent Dr. Jadranko Prlic. Now -- can you hear me, sir? Okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to move rather quickly because I have a lot of documents to go through. I don't mean to be rude but I'm going to be going at a rather fast pace. I just want to make sure before we start: You arrived somewhere in January 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started in Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 1st of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And you were there --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there until the 27th of July, with an interruption on leave between the 6th of May until the 26th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so you were rather new in August -- I mean in April; correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before -- before coming into the area you had an orientation?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not -- I did not get a briefing about the country, if I can summarise it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you get a briefing about who was who?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received this briefing in Siroki Brijeg through the CC Mostar at the time, so slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you get a briefing on the structure of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- I partially read up on it, and then also by asking questions, so yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it that you were able to look at the legislation that set up the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to see exactly the structure, how it was organised, who was responsible for what? Did you do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't have a look at the legislation. I don't have the laws, and I wouldn't have had the time, but the structures, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, how could you know about the structure without looking at the legislation that set it up?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give a reply to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a look at the outlines that I was given and looked at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell me what the Presidency did? What were their functions? I'm not talking about the president but the Presidency and how it was composed. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Presidency, if -- just to make terms clear, from -- compared to the German structure was responsible for the guidelines and policy for all military matters, political matters, et cetera. And Mr. Prlic was at the top of this government, and Mr. Zubak, if I remember rightly, was the vice-president. And there was a defence minister, deputy defence minister, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So if I understand you correctly, Mr. Prlic was in the -- was in the Presidency, and he being the president had all these functions based on what you were told or what you understood; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we're getting close to the terminology. Mr. Prlic, let me say is like this, he was the prime minister, the chancellor, the boss of the government of HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what was Mate Boban then?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, Mate Boban was like an overarching figure who understood everything and who was really responsible for the policy. And the others were the executor of his basic ideas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, did he have -- I mean -- okay. Germany has a president and it has a chancellor; right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I take it that if I were to go to Germany and look at the legislation, the constitution, I would be able to figure out who does what; right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather compare it to the French model. The elected President Sarkozy is Mate Boban and the government with the ministers is the government of Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it's your understanding, that based on that particular structure, the Prime Minister is in charge of the military? You know, somewhat like, say, for instance, the Italian model as opposed to the French model.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going back to the German model. In wartimes, the chancellor is also responsible for the armed forces, and this is, as is the case of war, the prime minister is also responsible for the armed forces, and his ministers support him in that task. But it doesn't have to be like that, but this was how I imagined it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, you mentioned the French when I mentioned the German. I mentioned the Italian, you went back to the German. So let's stick with one country. Is the president of Germany the supreme commander, especially in wartime? Is he the one that commands the military? Yes, no, I don't know?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he is not the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's the Chancellor.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, you said that in April you were new and around April 18th is when you attended this meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, the meeting, among other things, in West Mostar, but not as a participant but rather more as an observer. I was not in the conference room at Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, and I don't mean to be disrespectful, but given that you had no orientation, you had just arrived, that for all intents and purposes you knew little to nothing about what was happening there in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not dismissing any respect. When I arrived in the country, I felt quite lost, but slowly I tried to understand matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we had a witness here. His name was Watkins. Did you ever meet him, by any chance? Philip --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have met Philip Watkins.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he indicated that when he testified, he indicated that it took him several months to figure out what was happening. Would that be the case with you as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'm referring to, for the Court's convenience, page -- that exchange would be on pages 18908, all the way to 18910.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But that's not in your documents, sir. That's just for the Court. Just answer my question. Would that be with you as well?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I must confirm this. In order really to get a basic understanding it would probably take longer than -- the duration of any mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to get ahead of myself a little bit. I take it you spent a lot of time with Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't -- no, I didn't spend a lot of time with him, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You had a lot of meetings with him then?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were not so many that I can recollect. I can remember the first meeting quite well. There was also a further meeting that I can remember quite well. But otherwise, there were not that many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I mention this that because in looking at all the documents that the Prosecution gave us, I don't see anything where you had a meeting with Mr. Prlic, you as a representative of the European Community Monitoring Mission. I see nothing, not one single solitary report that you had a meeting and that an exchange took place. Nothing. Could it be, sir, that you didn't have any meetings with Mr. Prlic? And you're confused over the years?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't mix up anything. I personally never met Mr. Prlic, unlike with Mr. Stojic and also Mr. Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no personal interview or conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. To make sure, you never had any meetings with Mr. Prlic? That was a question. To make sure --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Sorry. I thought it was a -- I considered it a statement for the minutes or whatever, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The inflection wasn't there perhaps. The interpreters haven't got used to my English. So I take it that you never had a meeting with Mr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meeting or an encounter with other participants, yes, but not a personal encounter in the shape of a conversation, and I was not really encouraged to do that when I think back to the 18th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The 18th of May or the 18th of April?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this meeting in Mostar on the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to get a little ahead of myself. I'm just going to touch on this, on this meeting, and then we'll get back to it in more detail, but were you aware, sir, that there were two meetings actually on that particular day, one where General Halilovic was not present, and later on in the evening when General Halilovic was present, because he had been brought over by General Morillon, and in that second meeting which you talked about, Mr. Prlic was not present. And I mention this because you said you don't get things mixed up. So could you by chance be mixing meetings, and is it possible that you're mistaken?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there were several meetings, as I already said yesterday, and that there was also a change in positions geographically I already said yesterday, and I cannot -- I really didn't understand the content of the conferences nor the participants. Also, that I talked to Mr. Prlic in front of one of the conference rooms, I only learned about that in hindsight. I didn't get the name quite straight away at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Somebody told you that the person you'd been talking to, and Mr. Prlic, who everybody has indicated is rather urbane and rather serious and rather polite, he didn't introduce himself?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already stated, he possibly introduced himself and I myself, too, but I slowly learned how to pronounce names and to remember names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a slow process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on a little bit. The Vance-Owen Peace Plan, were you aware of the details of the plan?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the details are concerned, I'm quite prudent, but I knew about various provinces, 10, 8, 9, and had some documentation, who was the leading power, so to speak, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And on province 8, then you must have known that the Vance-Owen Peace Plan called for -- for province 8 for Mostar to be its capital.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now we're going to go through a series of very quick documents. 1D 01281. So that would be in the binder, in the blue binder. Yes. 1D 01281. This is a decision, and we can see it's dated 11 May, 1993. And in Article 1, it says: "The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina hereby accepts in full and shall ensure implementation of the documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan for Bosnia and Herzegovina." Were you aware of this decision, sir? And I'm asking the question because later on we'll see that ECMM was asked to play a role, but were you aware of this decision, that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had accepted in full for the implementation of the documents connected to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan? It's a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go to the next document. 1D 01338. Here's a conclusion. Again it's 11 May 1993, and we can see from the title: "Conclusions on the implementation of the documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan for Bosnia and Herzegovina." I take it you would have been aware of this as well. We don't need to go through it in any detail?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now we go to 1D 01594. Now, this is a document that predates those two. It's April 2, 1993, and you will see at the very bottom it's signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic. It's addressed to Mr. Thebault. I take it you knew this gentleman; right? He was your -- your boss, for all intents and purposes.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he was my boss.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And in this document we can see and I believe we might have seen this earlier in this courtroom, we see here in the very first line: "In accordance with your suggestions and expressed will to be directly engaged in the realisation of the agreement accepted by Alija Izetbegovic, a representative of the Muslim nation, and Mate Boban, a representative of the Croatian nation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, we were informed in our discussion on April 1, 1993, in Mostar by Mr. Christopher Beese and Mr. Enrique Salamanca de Garay, please be informed ... " And it goes on and so forth. Were you aware that Dr. Prlic had sent this letter in order to arrange a meeting and had in fact proposed various issues for discussion? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Suffice it to say on the April the 18th meeting that you attended or witnesses, you -- you were not involved in arranging that meeting in any fashion. You were just new and you just went along as an observer more or less; correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case I wasn't involved at the beginning of this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next document, 1D 01595. And this is about minutes from a meeting in Medjugorje in May 18, 1993, and this is between the delegation of the Republic of Croatia, and it lists all the other individuals that were involved in the meeting. I don't want to waste too much time on that, but if we go to paragraph number 3, it's numbered, it says: "The president of the Transitional Government of the RBiH, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, shall be Jadranko Prlic. In agreement with the Muslim side, he shall recommend a balanced government of eight ministerial portfolios of which three will remain without appointment. In case an agreement is impossible to reach he shall consult with the co-chairmen of the peace conference." It goes on to say: "Dr. Haris Silajdzic shall remain as Minister of Foreign Affairs and the deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs shall be a Croatian with equal rights as Minister Silajdzic." And then at the very bottom it talks about the -- we have the organisation for province Mostar, province Travnik, and the next page province Zenica. Sir, were you aware in light of your position, your location, the information that you were receiving, were you aware that Dr. Jadranko Prlic was proposed as the president of the transitional government of RBiH pursuant to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan and the implementation documents that we've just seen? Were you aware of that? It's a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good. Now, incidentally, do you know whether you or others in your mission consulted with Dr. Prlic in relation to his new position to see how he would go about in implementing or carrying out his task as president of the transitional government? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we go to the next document, 1D 01596. And incidentally, for the German interpreters who have just joined us, in case I'm going too fast, feel free to slow me down. May 21, 1993. This is a letter, again by Dr. Jadranko Prlic. We can see it's addressed to Mate Boban and Alija Izetbegovic. I'll just read a couple of things. The first paragraph it states: "Pursuant to the agreement reached in Medjugorje on May 18, 1993, regarding the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan in Bosnia and Herzegovina, I write to you in my capacity as the president of the transitional government of RBiH and request that as representatives of the Croatian and Muslim people, you partake in the consultation for the election of a transitional government." And then you can see from the very next sentence it talks about each side indicating who they wish to appoint to various positions. Now, were you -- and there's a deadline on the 3rd, or he wishes an a response by May 24th. Were you aware of Mr. Prlic's efforts with Mate Boban and Alija Izetbegovic to begin the implementation process? Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this letter from a different perspective, I know that the Muslim side was hesitating the give the names to complete the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And we're going to get there. I'm glad you mentioned that, because as I understand your testimony when my colleague Ms. Nozica was questioning you, you had indicated -- or it might have been the Prosecutor, that the Muslims were hesitant in the implementation of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. In English, we would say they were dragging their feet. One might even say that they really had no intention of carrying -- carrying on in good faith; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at the next document, 1D 01597. 1597. Again here we see May 23, 1993. If we look at the second page, you can see that it's by Dr. Jadranko Prlic as president of the government, and here this is a letter to the co-chairmen of the conference on former Yugoslavia, Mr. Owen and Mr. Stoltenberg. "Report on the undertaken activities of the president of the Transitional Central Government." And here we can see that he's giving them notice that he has begun the process. Were you aware of this? This basically --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not learned about the various -- the individual steps taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next document is 1D 01598. 1598, dated again, May, 23, 1993, signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic as president of the government, addressed to the government of RBiH. In its earlier composition, we see. That's how it's been translated. And the subject: "Handing over the mandate to the new government." And here, if we go through the middle of the first paragraph it says: "That it has been decided that I shall be the president of the government and shall commence with preparing its composition that shall be verified by the coordinating body. Since the time frames for these activities are very short, I think would serve the purpose if you were to commence with the preparation of the necessary documentation for the hand-over." And then further down, and again, I'm just going to skip over some of the language, it says: "Bearing in mind that a large number of employees will, in this new situation, find themselves without employment, I would request that you undertake all measures to assist these people having in mind their professional level, social and other aspects of their situation." So were you aware again that here was Dr. Jadranko Prlic writing to the Sarajevo government pursuant to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, of his intentions to go forward as was expected of him; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We turn to the next document 1D 01599. 1599. Again dated May 23, 1993. You see at the bottom signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, president of the government. This time it's addressed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, attention Dr. Haris Silajdzic. And here from the very first paragraph, in the middle of it says: "In accordance with this agreement, Dr. Jadranko Prlic is elected as president of the government, and you as the Minister of Foreign Affairs. In accordance with that, it would necessary that you inform -- that you inform of these facts the government, i.e., the ministries of foreign affairs of all the states in which the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina has established diplomatic relations." And then we see that Dr. Jadranko Prlic presents a short curriculum vitae, and at the very end we see the last sentence which says -- or last paragraph which says: "The government of the United States of America, Federal Republic of Germany and the European Community should also be informed that the ambassadors of Croatian nationality will be appointed soon." Were you aware of this, sir, you being with the UN mission at the time, were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about such a letter, but I know that I'd seen in overviews what nationalities the relative ambassadors should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We can go to the next document, P 0 -- P 02509. This is a Prosecution document, but what is absent, Your Honours, if you look at the second page of this document which is in B/C/S there is some sort of title, and I'm told it says "Announcement for public," and I don't want to take a chance in reading it because my language skills are challenging but that's what I'm told. It's sort of a public announcement, and we can see here again, at the very top, it says: "On 25th of May, 1993, the Presidency of the HDZ BiH rep held a meeting presided by Mate Boban. Actual events were taken into consideration, especially the obligations on the basis of the common statement signed by Mr. Boban and Mr. Izetbegovic on the 25th of April in Zagreb, including concrete implementation of Vance-Owen Plan concluded on 18th of May, 1993, in Medjugorje." And then we see that appointments are being made and suggested. Were you aware of this since this was a public announcement, albeit it is in the Croatian language? Would this have come to your attention by any chance?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether this was a public notice or not I don't know, but I do know this document. I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we go, Your Honours, at the very end of the document you will note that the public announcement states: "With this nomination, the Croat side have carried out their duties and after nomination of representatives from the Muslim population in the provinces 8, 9 and 10 can begin peaceful life, life of protected human rights and stronger defence from the aggressor." And we see at the bottom it's -- it's the 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I point this out because of the earlier statement that you made that apparently, at least from what you were able to glean and understand and appreciate at the time, the Muslims were less than cooperative or less than willing to carry out their duties, and that is to nominate their representatives to fill the positions in provinces 8, 9, and 10 so that the implementation process would begin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at the next document, 1D 01600, 1600. This is dated May 27th, 1993. And here we see at the bottom it's president of the Presidency of RBiH, and it's Alija Izetbegovic. It's addressed to Dr. Jadranko Prlic. Subject, consultation for establishment of the transitional government. I just wish to point out a couple of things. And it might be -- it will become relevant with the next document. Here under paragraph number 1 there's an acknowledgement that yes, indeed, "We have agreed in Medjugorje that you are a candidate for the first prime minister of the government of RBiH." Then if we go on to the second one, paragraph number 2: "In order to propose to you the candidates, it is necessary for me to know for which portfolios it would be good that you propose their distribution. We are, among other things, of course, interested in the ministry for refugees (because of large number of Muslim refugees)." And this is dated the 27th of May, 1993. Were you aware of -- of President Izetbegovic's communication back to Mr. Jadranko Prlic -- Dr. Jadranko Prlic concerning his earlier letter to him? Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about this, but I imagine that I had read some sort of summary of this later, but not at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The next document is very quick. 1D 01601, again signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic as president of the government, dated June 1, 1993, in Mostar, and here he is giving his greetings. "The president of the transitional central government of the RBiH, Dr. Jadranko Prlic, has on the occasion of the Muslim religious holiday Kurban Bajram expressed his best wishes to all the clerical dignitaries and the Islam congregation ... " and it goes on giving his particular greetings. Were you aware of this gesture by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, back in June 1, 1993, in his capacity as president of the government, of the interim government?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean not the Vance-Owen Plan but in the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... He's with -- I'm just --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I ask a question whether we have the same document. This is the 7th Muslim Brigade or do I have the wrong document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It's 1D 01601. 1601. If you don't have it, I can give you my copy. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's it. If you don't have it, we can assist you. It might be easier to just hand you the copy so we can move on because I'm under tremendous time constraints.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I have it. 1601.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And again I just read it out. It's dated June 1, 1993. These are greetings from Dr. Jadranko Prlic as president of the government, if we look at the signature down there. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we look at the next document 1D 01602, 1602. And here again at the bottom, Dr. Jadranko Prlic, president of the government, if we look at the top, it says 5 May, but the May has been crossed out, Your Honours, and then it says June, handwritten, 1993. Hence the order. Do you see that? Do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah. And this is addressed to Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban, and I wish to point out here, consistent to the earlier document where Mr. -- President Izetbegovic expressed in particular that he wished the Ministry of Refugees to go to the Muslim nation, and of course, we know by virtue of the arrangement that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would remain with the Muslims. We see in the second paragraph, it says, "In accordance with expressed interest, a need for appointment of balanced government, it is my opinion that the division of portfolios should be as follows: Muslims, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry for Refugee Issues, and Ministry of Communication and Transport." And then we see for the Croats, president of the government which Dr. Jadranko Prlic holds, then Ministry of Reconstruction and Ministry of International Trade. And then, of course, they also allow three different ministries to the Serbs to be filled at some later point. So were you aware of this, that Dr. Jadranko Prlic, consistent with or in accordance with President Izetbegovic's wishes, went ahead and made this proposal?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, just to -- just to hammer the point home, at the very bottom, if we look at the second to last, second-to-last paragraph, you see that Dr. Jadranko Prlic saying, "I'm asking you for your agreement with these proposals," and then he goes on to say, "I expect that you will propose more candidates for each existing position no later than Tuesday, June 10, 1993, since I have the obligation to form the government within three days, and the meeting with the co-presidents of the peace conference on former Yugoslavia of June 3." So you see that.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And would it not be, I mean, you could draw an educated conclusion from all this that Dr. Jadranko Prlic is moving, with all deliberate speed, to form the government as was expected to him, in order to put in process a peace plan that would at least -- well, that they were hoping would stop the fighting at least between the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I intervene? [Interpretation] Witness, if you look at this, Mr. Prlic says that he wants to have proposals by the 10th of June, because until the 3rd of -- three days before the 3rd he has to propose a government. Is that something you can understand? Can you explain to me what that meant in practical terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, can I say first of all, Your Honour, that I don't know all of these documents because these were far above the level I was at the time, and I only know things of a more verbal nature about the events of the time, except for the files with names in them. But these are procedures would have been instigated very shortly after this letter. But the 18th of May was considerably before this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may -- if I may, the -- I'm told that the translation is a little awkward, and so -- it says, "Since I took" - as opposed to "I have" - "I took the obligation to form the government within three days at the meeting with the co-presidents of the peace conference of the former Yugoslavia on June 3." So in other words the meeting took place on June 3, and that's when he took that obligation on. And we can certainly have the document retranslated, Your Honours, to clarify that point. The last document, at least in this -- for this chapter is P 02490. 2490. This is a Prosecution document. It's dated 22 May, 1993, and it's -- it's generated by the EC Monitor Mission, Danish delegation, Greater Serbia, and if we go to the -- at the end, I believe it's at the end. No, I'm sorry. On the very first page we can see that -- that this was sent off by Ole Brix Andersen and of course you knew Mr. Andersen, did you not? On the very first page --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before? It's a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It seems very familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And just very briefly because I just want to point this out, it would appear if we look at the first page, flip the -- I'm sorry, page number 1, which would be the second page, we see this is a proposal for ECMM participation in the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan, and -- now, were you by any chance, given that you were located in an area where you might be put in a position to implement the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, were you aware of this proposal, that's number one, and number two, did you have anything to do with the drafting of this proposal? In other words, did they solicit your input and guidance and wisdom in drafting a proposal?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not in the drafting a proposal, but in the implementation. And the practical matters for us, we were further down the rung of the ladder, was, for example, that we spoke to Muslim leaders and asked them why they hadn't done anything yet. And I recall that at some phase, I can't define the date, Mr. Cibo was one of the people I spoke to about it. And I had heard, in general, that he was appointed by Mr. Izetbegovic as a sort of commissioner, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And one would think, would they not - I mean, logic would follow, at least mine does - that if he was appointed by President Izetbegovic that Mr. Cibo would follow Mr. Izetbegovic's instructions.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what one should assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if Mr. Cibo was dragging his feet, being uncooperative, being non-responsive, being unwilling to go ahead and participate in the implementation of the plan, one might further conclude that perhaps that's exactly why he was placed there by Mr. Izetbegovic, for that very same purpose. Unless of course Mr. Izetbegovic was totally unaware of what Mr. Cibo was up to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to that question. I think that calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman certainly can answer the question, especially based in part on his previous answer, but if the -- if the Judges think that the question is argumentative in the form, which it may be, then I can certainly move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, before the objection was raised you said that you met with Mr. Cibo. When you discussed with him about the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan on the Muslim side, did he convey the impression that he was enthusiastic or rather reserved, that he was overwhelmed? What kind of impression did he make on you as to his position, his stance with regard to the implementation? We've just seen, through numerous documents, that on the Croat side they were moving ahead very rapidly. So what did Mr. Cibo say to you exactly, without any sort of hypothesis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I met Mr. Cibo on the 5th of May, and we talked together for several hours on the Spanish transport vehicle. We talked about various things including the Vance-Owen Plan. I don't remember the exact wording. The situation was a situation on the terrain, so to speak, but I do remember that he was reserved, and he did not show any enthusiasm. One could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we look at this document just very quickly, just a couple of points, on the very -- on that page number one we see under item number 4 or paragraph that is numbered 4, we say -- we see here that at the meeting it was agreed that the Vance-Owen Plan should be -- should be implemented to the extent possible considering the character of the provinces, and then it mentions provisions, and present circumstances within the three regions, Mostar, Travnik, Zenica. So I take it your understanding was those were the regions where the Vance-Owen Peace Plan was going to be implemented; correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then we see that at least the ECMM is saying that "The international community needs to take rapid and positive action with concrete results demonstrated in order to convince the parties that the agreement reached is viable." Okay? So I take it you also understood that you, along with others, for all intents and purposes, the international community, had to assist in this implementation process, hence why you were meeting with people such as Mr. Cibo to cajole him into getting himself into action; correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting resulted from different circumstances, but the opportunity was there to talk to him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the reason why you were talking to him about it was because you had an obligation. At least -- at least somebody who was above you, Ole Brix Andersen, is making this proposal. He certainly seems to think that ECMM and others in the international community must take action; right? And that's what you were doing.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must think of the time frame. When I was together with Mr. Cibo for a long time, things hadn't developed so far, as far as I recall, but things were moving. And again I met Mr. Cibo once more. I don't remember the exact time, but it was when the implementation process started, and this was one of the subjects, especially because I knew him from the beginning of April, and it was something I was very much aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we again look at page number 2, we just see at the very bottom it says "Tasks in the two agreements," and we see under paragraph that is numbered 13, "Agreement on interim arrangements". I don't want to go through -- through any of that, but it seems at least - and there is a purpose I did it in this fashion - that here we are in May and I showed you documents before that that were back in -- in June, so as early as May, the ECMM was gearing up for the implementation, and then we see June. We see Dr. Jadranko Prlic moving pursuant to what was expected of him; correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We can now off on to another -- another area, and that has to do with the convoys. Yesterday you were asked a few questions about convoy, and I just wanted to clarify a few points. Now, there was a Makarska Agreement that was on 10 July 1993, and if I am correct, the ECMM was not present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, briefly I just want to go through a chronology before we go through some documents, and to the best of your recollection, if you could tell me whether my chronology is consistent with your memory. If not, we'll deal with it through some other means, perhaps with you, perhaps with others, but I've indicated, number one, that on 10 July 1993 there was the Makarska Agreement. And incidentally, that agreement dealt with convoys, and we've seen it here before in P 03346 just to let the Court know. It's not there. It's not in your bundle. I'm just letting the Court know. So that agreement dealt with convoys; correct? With the issue of humanitarian relief. If you recall. You're shaking are head. We need to make a record.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. I'm terribly sorry. I was trying to concentrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Then on 13 July 1993, the ABiH attacked in the area of Dubrava plateau region, Stolac, Capljina, Buna. And again we saw that in another document and that would be P 03427, Your Honours, earlier. But do you recall that three days later, 13 July, the ABiH carried out an attack? Do you recall that? If you don't recall, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not particularly Stolac, but the 3rd of July, this was after the 30th of July -- June where the fighting was continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no. But what I'm asking is -- what I'm saying is this: 10th July you have Makarska Agreement. 13th July, three days later, the army of BiH attacks in the area of Dubrava plateau, the region of Stolac, Capljina, Buna. Were you aware of that? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I ask you whether you're talking about the document or the fact? Are you talking about a paper, because I don't remember a paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So a period of time is in the area where there were uprisings of the armija and there was fighting, but then it quietened down somewhat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then on 14th of July, 1993, were you aware that an UNHCR convoy was cancelled? And again that can be found on P 03453 [Realtime transcript read in error "P 05453"] for the Court but were you aware that on 14 July 1993, an UNHCR convoy was cancelled? It's a yes or no --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Nobody's expecting you by the way. It's a long period of time. That's why we have some documents, hopefully might clarify the point and on 14 July 1993, Dr. Jadranko Prlic sent a letter to the UNHCR, and that's going to be found on 1D 01336 which we'll get to, but were you aware of that, that Dr. Jadranko Prlic sent a letter? And there's a purpose for all of this by the way. We'll get to it.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then on 15 July there was still heavy fighting in the Buna area south of Mostar. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that the fighting continued, and as I said before, we didn't have findings of our own on this, but we heard signs of heavy fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm truly -- I apologise for interrupting here, but just for the record at line 12, the reference to P 05453, I think that is incorrect. It should be P 3453.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Either I'm tired, which is probably the case, or I was misheard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In any event -- okay. Now, we have the Makarska Agreement. There's another -- there is an agreement. We can find that on 3346, P 03346. I think we looked at it yesterday very briefly. I don't know if you have it in your packet. But it's in the Prosecution binder. The Prosecution's. That's the very thick one. And I just want to point something out very quickly. 3346.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we see -- we see it sort in the middle it talks about recalling the Medjugorje agreement concluded on 18 May 1993. Were you aware what that agreement was all about?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know the agreement, but I can put it into the context of the question -- in the context of the question raised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that is that it was -- the agreement was basically -- again dealt with convoys and what-have-you; right? In that context. Okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then if we go to the very last page or the second-to-last page, we see who is nominated and we see there representative of the Croatian Defence Council, we see Dr. Jadranko Prlic, president of HVO Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna, and then we see Zubak and other names as well. And then we see other names. Okay. Now, if we could just move on, real quickly, to the next document. Again, this is a Prosecution document. 3427, 3427. This is a document that was shown to you, I believe, yesterday. It's dated 13 July 1993, and I just want to point out something, couple of things actually, and at the very end it says, "Best Regards, CC Mostar". So you would be familiar with this document. Here we see that there's a meeting with a Mr. Zubak. Do you have it? Do you have the document, sir? Okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then we see sort of in the middle of that first paragraph, it says, "He agreed that the current fighting could again interrupt the possibilities for convoys, as already Mr. Tadic had said, he stressed that BiH has not announced the responsible person for the convoys." And so now, were you aware that Mr. Zubak was raising this issue? In other words, that the fighting is preventing the convoys to go through, and that as Mr. Tadic is saying, that the Muslim side had not announced the responsible person for the convoys.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the last thing was something I heard from Mr. Tadic himself in addition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you were present at this, were you not?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This document was generated by you, I believe, and I believe that you were present at the time and having a conversation with Mr. Zubak. So you would have heard Zubak saying that he agreed that the current fighting could again interrupt the possibilities for convoys. So he's stating the reasons why perhaps convoys may not come through; right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we go to the second --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, go ahead. I don't mean to cut you off. I thought you were finished.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was also because of the fighting. We talked about the fighting already at the north of Jablanica towards Prozor, and when they were talking about fighting, it was a matter of course that there were no convoys, and military convoys themselves couldn't get through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And that -- and that incidentally might be one of the reasons why convoys of humanitarian aid are unable to get through, if there's fighting, especially if one of the two sides is activating the fighting. I mean, that makes sense; right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really go into the subject of who was the initiator in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you who the initiator is. All I'm saying is if there's fighting -- I mean, it's one thing to say the government or the -- or the person who's responsible is not allowing convoys to go through. It's another thing to say that the passage is blocked because of fighting going on; right? There are two different issues; right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go to the second page, under military matters, paragraph -- it's number 3, "Military activity", we see there, "There are gun positions now one kilometre north of Siroki Brijeg firing this morning and in the middle of the day. There have been army attacks in the area of Dubrava plateau, what is the region of Stolac-Capljina-Buna." So it would seem that at least you are aware that three days after there is an agreement signed here is the armija carrying out an offensive. And I say offensive because they're -- it would appear that they're the ones initiating the fighting; correct? You wrote this, so ...

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now we go to the next document -- sorry, did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, figure 3, the first sentence refers of course to the positions of the HVO. The second sentence has to do with indications from UNPROFOR and the UNMO officers and what our team itself had heard in terms of sounds of fighting. So this is how this passage emerged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay. And you wrote it.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in fact at the bottom of the page where it says "Assessment", you even note that Mr. Zubak has made an offer for you to meet with Mr. Prlic; correct? The very last sentence under "Assessment". "The offer to meet Mr. Prlic is an additional indicator for that." I should say, actually, you've mentioned that earlier and this is part of your assessment.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, if we go to the next document, 3453. 3453. This is dated July 14. And if we go to the second page under (D), Southern BH Command, it says here, "(1) Mostar, all UNPROFOR vehicle movement towards Mostar continued to be forbidden. Both sides -- both sides' sources state that combat are taking place in the Buna area and south of Mostar. SA fire and explosions have been recorded in Capljina surroundings. The access has been denied to UNPROFOR vehicles. HVO continues gathering personnel and material for a further offensive, and an UNHCR convoy that was going to deliver humanitarian aid to Muslim refugees in the Heliodrom in Mostar has been cancelled by UNHCR due to the combat and the incidents that have taken place in Capljina. The population is blaming UNPROFOR for not having prevented the recent events." Now, would it be fair to say, based on this passage, that that convoy that was headed towards the Heliodrom was prevented from going there as a result of the fighting, the activity that was going on?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the fighting and also the factor that the access was prevented so that -- that the Spanish Battalion was escorting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say access prevented, do you think it would have been wise to -- in the middle of a war zone where there's fighting going on and you told us how on one mission, you just turned around and left as soon as there was some shooting going on, do you think it would have been wise to drive a convoy of humanitarian aid through the middle of fighting where both sides are waging war? Or would the safer course be cancel and wait for another day?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be right to cancel it, but in June, for example, I'd like to point out that sniping activities were there in East Mostar, and still the Spanish were able to enter East Mostar in spite of admittedly small-scale fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll move on. 1D 01336. This is a letter signed by Jadranko Prlic, president of the HVO. It's 1 -- it's the other -- the blue binder. There you go. 1D 01336. It's dated 14 July 1993. So this would have been the following day. Remember I indicated that there was a letter sent by Jadranko Prlic, and here if we look in the middle of the -- the second paragraph it says: "However, the attack of the Muslim forces on the large area of Mostar and Capljina, including the main road Capljina-Mostar (the section belonging to the only corridor from Ploce to Bosnia) is a flagrant proof of their unwillingness to respect the agreement." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So let me put it to you this way: If one side wanted to prevent that convoy from through, one way would be to engage in military activities to block the corridor; right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Next document is Prosecution P 03470. It's -- yeah, that's that one. 3470. And this is dated 15 July 1993. This was not shown to you, but it's a Prosecution document. I'm told that -- I'm told that it was shown to you. And if we just look at very briefly under number 3, "Military activity". You say: "As M2 could hear from Siroki Brijeg last night, heavy weapon fire -- heavy weapons fire from the direction of Buna, fighting continues south of Mostar. They also could see smoke today in the direction of the area of Buna. The military police in the CP of Varda told M2 that the armija is at present shelling with mortars the road from Siroki Brijeg to Mostar, although they did not say in which place." "M3 reported that all the Muslim soldiers in Tomislavgrad were disarmed and sent back to their homes yesterday (about 400-500)." Were you aware of this military activity as was reported in this document? And this is 15 of July, five days after the agreement that was signed to allow the convoys to go through. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a report that my deputy prepared at a time when I was not there. I read it afterwards and talked to him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether your deputy made any efforts to find out why the Muslim side were carrying out these activities only five days or three days after they had signed an agreement that would bring vital humanitarian aid to the Muslim population, why they were waging attacks blocking a corridor? Do you know whether your deputy or whoever was working there made any efforts to get to the bottom of this?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his attempts were especially geared towards creating access to Mostar. He didn't manage that. And then he didn't have access to -- from the south either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So are you saying to me that -- that ECMM did not have access at all to the Muslim side to find out -- I mean, you had access to Cibo, so I take it you're saying that there was no way to find out, if not maybe in the Mostar Muslim authority, but perhaps go through Izetbegovic, and find out why after such an agreement is signed to allow vital humanitarian aid to go through, why his military wing, representing his party and his people is waging war? I mean, you told us how he was dragging his feet with the implementation of Vance-Owen.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could this be one of those examples?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be, but once more if -- well, convoys are stopped for minor reasons. If you think of a check-point, a small check-point with two people with guns and it stops a convoy, you don't need combat activity. If the convoys -- if the check-points are there, they can stop everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm fully aware of that, but that wasn't -- that wasn't the answer to a question that I had posed, but never mind. We'll go on to the next document. We're going to switch topics a little bit, and we're going to document 3361. I believe this was shown to you yesterday. And I also have the transcript where it was -- where you made reference to it. But what was posed to you or a question that was posed to you was whether you would have of been aware of documents or documents of this sort as a matter of routine, and you indicated, yes, we received these reports and used them.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go to -- under the third page under 4 where it says BritBat sector, there is a section there. We can skip over that a little bit because we don't have time. But we go under C, Travnik. It says: "The BiH OG command, Alagic, said to the ICRC that he had given orders that no prisoners were to be taken by his troops." And then there's a comment. But my question is did you react to that? You being a military man, you coming in possession of these documents and, as you said, you used them albeit it's not in your direct vicinity, were you -- did you react in any way? I mean, how could a military commander advise his troops not to take any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't react to that. It was far beyond my area of responsibility, and there were enough people there to do something. There were -- if I had tried to do anything, I would have been intervening in their work and interrupted their work, and I wouldn't have been able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS JOHANN NISSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because to read such a document, of course, it takes a certain time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You could have said, "Listen, I think something has to be done." I mean, there are Geneva Conventions; right? So -- but be that as it may, I only bring this out because it was repeatedly brought out by my learned friend on the Prosecution side how you would get these documents and how you would use them. But now let's look at two documents I think that might be helpful, and this goes to another issue that may not directly involve you, but it involves a section of the indictment. It's 1D 01605.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment before you move on. You have already used one hour and 15 minutes. Who has given you additional time to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No one. No one, Your Honour. I can stop at this point, but there are just two documents that I wish to show the gentleman directly related to my previous question, and I think that that would be -- I could end at that. If we could look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Well, proceed until 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
